baseline.name: Recursive build with inorder linear searches
baseline.approach: For each subtree root, scan its inorder range to locate the split.
baseline.space: O(h) recursion plus O(n) returned nodes

archived.name: Direct value-to-inorder lookup
archived.space: O(V+h) auxiliary storage plus O(n) returned nodes

why: A precomputed bounded-domain index replaces repeated inorder scans with constant-time root-position lookup.
quantitative_comparison: The baseline can inspect n+(n-1)+...+1 inorder positions on a skewed case. The archive initializes V slots and maps/constructs each of n nodes once. No timing ratio follows from those counts.
tradeoffs: Extra fixed lookup storage may dominate tiny inputs. Unique values in -3000..3000 and matching traversals are required; recursion remains O(n) in a skewed tree and allocations are unchecked.
evidence_basis: Static source comparison to repeated inorder search, with bounded-domain assumptions explicit; no measured benchmark.
